pre_mortem: It is Monday and the SEA@WAS slip lost. Path one: Washington sold out to Smith-Njigba after 122 and 155, Cross's backup was fine, the middle 13.1 YPA was ten throws of noise, and Seattle led 17-3 so Darnold threw under 25 times while Price and Wilson ran. He finished in the 60s and 91.5 lost. Path two, which can hit on the same night or the other night: Mariota kept it close, Washington ran to protect him with Cosmi out, Daniels' carries transferred to Croskey-Merritt, and he went 18 for 55 against a two-game 3.73 YPC sample that did not hold, especially if Pili sat. The parlay needs the base and loses if either flip arrives, because the competitive flip feeds Croskey-Merritt and the blowout flip starves Smith-Njigba. Those counters are why both legs are flagged and unsized. They are not clearly stronger than the pre-kick reads, Cross out plus 10.46 YPA on 26 right-side throws for Smith-Njigba, and Cosmi plus Daniels plus 3.73 YPC for the Croskey-Merritt under, so they are not cut.
slip_story: One SEA@WAS story, the base script, not a mix of opposites: Seattle leads but still throws to Smith-Njigba against Washington's soft right and a backup safety, and Washington on Mariota without Cosmi cannot keep the 14-carry Croskey-Merritt role against a 3.73 YPC front, so the rush under is the same lead, not a separate game. Price over needs the blowout clock-kill that can kill 91.5, and a Diggs or McLaurin over needs Washington to move the ball on a defense that has allowed no explosives, which is flip 1, the flip that also threatens the Croskey-Merritt under. No touchdown legs, no passing-yard or reception markets, one market per player, no depth receiver. Two legs, not padded to four.
